topic: Dimensional Leap: The Geometry of Non-Square Matrices
target_audience: Undergraduate students in Linear Algebra or Computer Science

sections.title: The Bridge Between Worlds: Introduction
lecture_lines: Square matrices transform space within the same dimension.
Non-square matrices move vectors between different dimensions.
Matrix columns show where input basis vectors land.
animations: Show a standard 2D grid centered at the origin. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Apply a 2x2 transformation, shearing the grid. (Color: #00FF00)
Display a 3x2 matrix next to the grid. (Color: #FFFF00)
Transition the 2D grid into a 3D plane. (Color: #00FFFF)
Highlight columns of the matrix as basis vectors in 3D. (Color: #FF00FF)

sections.title: Prerequisite Check: The DNA of a Matrix
lecture_lines: Columns represent the number of input basis vectors.
Rows represent coordinates needed in the output space.
This mapping defines the dimension of the transformation.
animations: Animate i-hat and j-hat unit vectors on 2D grid. (Color: #FF0000, #00FF00)
Display a matrix; highlight its columns with specific colors. (Color: #FFA500)
Show vector [x, y] as a linear combination of columns. (Color: #FFFFFF)

sections.title: Tall Matrices: Upgrading Dimensions (2D to 3D)
lecture_lines: A 3x2 matrix maps 2D input to 3D output.
Two input basis vectors land in a 3D world.
This creates a flat plane slicing through 3D space.
The transformation embeds the lower dimension into higher space.
Notice how the 2D grid lifts into the room.
animations: Show a 2D plane with a simple character figure. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Display a 3D coordinate frame with light gray axes. (Color: #808080)
Map the 2D plane onto a tilted 3D plane. (Color: #00FF00)
Highlight that the output lacks volume, remaining a plane. (Color: #FFFF00)
Label the two columns of the 3x2 matrix. (Color: #FF00FF)

sections.title: Wide Matrices: The Great Squashing (3D to 2D)
lecture_lines: A 2x3 matrix maps 3D input to 2D output.
Three basis vectors are squashed into a 2D plane.
This process inevitably involves losing one dimension of information.
Think of it as projecting a 3D bird's shadow.
The Null Space contains vectors that collapse to zero.
animations: Create a 3D cube representing a higher-dimensional input. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Show a 2D shadow plane positioned underneath the cube. (Color: #808080)
Flatten the 3D cube into a 2D square shadow. (Color: #FF0000)
Display a 2x3 matrix with 3 input columns. (Color: #FFFF00)
Highlight the vertical axis collapsing into a single point. (Color: #00FFFF)

sections.title: Summary & The 'Grid' Intuition
lecture_lines: Columns count input dimensions; rows count output dimensions.
Tall matrices embed space; wide matrices project and squash.
Non-square matrices are geometric bridges across dimensions.
animations: Display text: Rows = Output Dim, Columns = Input Dim. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Side-by-side view: 2D->3D (Tall) vs 3D->2D (Wide). (Color: #00FF00, #FF0000)
Final morphing grid visualizing dimension-to-dimension bridges. (Color: #FFFF00)
